title: deterministic-ingest-ids-trace-log-reconciliation-for-sli-debugging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently receive tickets where a tenant sees an SLO regression in the console but we cannot deterministically reproduce the exact ingest path because logs and traces for the same logical request are assigned different ingestion IDs across retries, aggregator shards, or after backfill replays. This makes post-hoc forensics noisy: dashboards show per-ingest_id metrics, runbook queries return fragmented traces, and alert investigations require manual stitching by correlating timestamps and attributes.

Goal: Introduce a deterministic ingest_id that is computed at the first gateway/edge hop and carried through the analytics ingestion pipeline (Kafka message header -> ingestor -> transform workers -> compacted store) so that any derived artifacts (logs, spans, events) from the same logical request share the same stable identifier. Use this to enable robust trace/log reconciliation, reproducible SLI delta checks, and a new 'replay-to-trace' debugging flow in Console.

Scope: 
- Compute a stable ingest_id at the API gateway for all console analytics traffic and for synthetic probes. The ingest_id must be collision-resistant at the tenant+time+nonce level and stable across retries for identical client payloads.
- Propagate ingest_id as a Kafka header and include it in the proto payloads where feasible.
- Update consumer services (ingestor, transformer, aggregator) to preserve the ingest_id and persist it in the compact event store index for downstream queries.
- Add reconciliation tooling and dashboards: (1) a reconciliation view that shows counts of unique ingest_ids vs. unique trace_ids per tenant over a sliding window, (2) a replay comparator that replays historical messages and verifies deterministic id generation and mapping.
- Provide backward compatibility: if ingest_id is missing, existing behavior continues and services must generate a best-effort deterministic id (based on available fields) while marking it as generated.

Constraints & non-goals:
- We will not change customer-facing telemetry formats (Console UI payloads) beyond adding the ability to display ingest_id in debug view.
- This ticket does not address cross-account trace redaction or downstream retention policy changes — follow-up work will handle retention+index costs.

Design decisions considered:
1) Centralized ID service vs. deterministic client-side computation: we chose deterministic computation (HMAC over tenant_id|timestamp_bucket|payload_fingerprint with optional server nonce) to avoid an extra RPC hop at high QPS and to make replays idempotent.
2) Where to persist ingest_id: store as a top-level indexed field in the event compact store to keep query costs predictable.
3) Header propagation vs. embedding in payload: use both (Kafka header + payload field) for consumer resilience; header takes precedence.

Compatibility & migration plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): inject ingest_id at gateway for 5% of tenants in us-west-2 and kafka topic x-analytics-v2. Consumers will log mismatches and emit metrics but not fail on missing ids.
- Phase 2 (wider rollout): increase to 50% and deploy transformer/aggregator changes to persist ingest_id to compact store. Add reconciliation dashboard.
- Phase 3 (complete): 100% rollout, enable replay comparator for on-demand forensic runs, deprecate best-effort id generation after 90 days.

Operational considerations:
- Metric budget: add a new metric analytics.ingest_id.mismatch and analytics.ingest_id.missing to SLO dashboards and a critical alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% for more than 10 minutes.
- Cost: indexing one additional 16-byte field will increase monthly storage index costs; product will evaluate retention and cardinality-first filters to limit explosion.
- Security: ingest_id must not contain PII; computed HMAC will use a per-cluster secret managed by KMS.

Deliverables:
- Gateway change: deterministic ingest_id computation + injection into Kafka header (PR #TBD)
- Consumer updates: ingestor/transformer/aggregator changes to preserve and persist ingest_id; tests and migration scripts (PRs #TBD)
- Dashboards: reconciliation view, mismatch heatmap, per-tenant ingest_id cardinality panels (Grafana/Console)
- Runbook entries for investigating ingest_id mismatches and for rolling back the gateway injection.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway computes a stable ingest_id for canary tenants and injects it into Kafka headers
At least one transformer and the compact store persist ingest_id and make it queryable via the analytics store API
Reconciliation dashboard shows expected ratio of trace_ids to ingest_ids and alerts on anomalies
Replay comparator can deterministically replay a historical batch and verify id stability for >= 99.9% of replayed messages in canary
No customer-facing errors are introduced in canary; mismatch metric remains below 0.5%
Security review completed and KMS keys provisioned for HMAC secrecy
notes: Initial spike found that using tenant_id + hour_bucket + sha256(payload_bytes)[0:8] + cluster_nonce yields stable, low-collision ids
Discussed with privacy team on 2026-02-24; confirmed no customer payloads are stored in plain in the id, use HMAC with KMS key
Related infra ticket: ENG-32101 (kafka-header-retention-config) must be merged before Phase 2 rollout

2026-03-07 - Design review (Samir Gupta): UX agreed to add ingest_id in the Console debug panel and a copy-to-clipboard button for support engineers.

2026-03-09 - Marco Chen: Deployed gateway change to canary (5% tenants in us-west-2). Initial mismatch rate observed: 0.12% over 6 hours. Investigating two mismatch classes: legacy mobile SDKs and synthetic probes without payload bytes.
